properties.name: Oakwood Bottoms & Turkey Bayou Campground
properties.fee_text: Turkey Bayou is a no-fee campground. Donationas are accepted by Friends of Turkey Bayou, who help maintain the campground and support the annual fishing derby. Hunting licenses & fees follow Illinois State law. For more information and to obtain hunting licenses, tags, waterfowl stamps, etc. visit Illinois Dept. of Natural Resources website .

fee_evidence_records.text: A favorite with waterfowl hunters, Oakwood Bottoms offers so much more from excellent bird watching to fishing opportunities and primitive camping at Turkey Bayou Campground. Picnic with your family or youth group at Oakwood Bottoms picnic site and take a short walk into the bottoms on the wooden boardwalk trail that loops back to the picnic area. The site also has a large picnic shelter next to a large pond, where you can enjoy watching ducks and other birds visit the pond in search of food. Big Muddy Boat Launch also offers one of the few locations to launch your boat or kayak onto the Big Muddy River. Visit our Oakwood Bottoms Hunting Page for hunting regulations, current flood compartment map and the Designated Waterfowl Refuge restrictions.

Big Muddy boat launch and Turkey Bayou campground are temporarily closed due to flooding. Designated Waterfowl Refuge Area Closed 14 days prior to start of waterfowl hunting season (Illinois' southern central zone) to the end of waterfowl hunting season. No walking access or hunting is permitted during the closure period in the designated waterfowl refuge.

properties.fee_text: Campsites $10/night - 8 people & 2 vehicles max. Payment cash or check only.

fee_evidence_records.text: Pine Hills campground has level campsites with open grassy areas between campsites. Popular with hunters in the spring and fall, the campground is also ideal for those who like to view nature, go birding, hike or take a scenic drive. Pine Hills Road leads to the top of the bluffs and features panoramic views of the LaRue Swamp and Mississippi River floodplain. Located adjacent to one of the largest natural areas in the state Pine Hills is ideal for nature lovers. In addition the Snake Road, located at the bottom of the bluffs is closed biannually to vehicular traffic, to protect the thousands of the reptiles and amphibians as they migrate between their summer and winter habitats. Pine Hills Campground Map

Camp only at designated campsites. Camping is not allowed in LaRue Pine Hills Research Natural Area. Pets are allowed only on a leash. Stay on the designated trail. Pack it in, Pack it out, along trails. Collections of any kind is strictly prohibited within the Research Natural Area. Violators will be prosecuted. Refer to the Illinois Dept. of Natural Resources hunting website for all hunting and fishing regulations .

fee_evidence_records.text: This campground is the site of an old Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) work camp. Somewhat off the beaten path Camp Cadiz is usually quiet and rarely do the campsites fill up; with the exception of turkey and deer hunting seasons. The campsites are level and each has a fire ring with grill and picnic table. Equestrian camping is allowed. Recreation Area Brochure/Map

Camp only at designated campsites. Pets are allowed only on a leash. Stay on the designated trail. Pack it in, Pack it out, along trails. A complete list of site regulations is posted on bulletin boards and at fee stations.

properties.name: Tower Rock Campground

fee_evidence_records.text: Located along the banks of the Ohio River, Tower Rock Campground offers beautiful scenery and close proximity to water activities like fishing and boating. The 1/4 mile trail can be accessed near the boat launch. Be aware this area is prone to flooding when river levels fluctuate.

No trash receptacles - No garbage pick-up provided. Pack it in - Pack it out. Camping is free and limited to 14 continuous days. Dogs allowed but must be leashed. Fishing regulations are set by Illinois Dept. of Natural Resources. Anglers can obtain fishing licenses on line .
